items.problem: The page's canonical is https://web.dev/articles/http-cache, and in this run a plain fetch of that URL (no Accept-Language) was redirected to the French ?hl=fr version. A crawler that follows the canonical may store the page in a language the reader did not ask for.
items.fix: Serve the canonical URL in its default language to clients that send no Accept-Language, and keep the language variants on hreflang alternates.

items.problem: Under "Common caching patterns" an h3 reads "Validation", the same text as the earlier h2. Up to 2.102 this chunker took it for that h2 and filed the rest of the section under "Validation"; 2.103 follows the h2 order and keeps it in #21, but any splitter that matches headings by their text alone still makes that cut, and a passage that says "Validation" with no subject is ambiguous to a retriever either way.
items.fix: Give the h3 its own name, such as "Validating cache-busted files", and open the passage with its subject.
items.before: Don't forget to set the Last-Modified and ETag headers, so that you don't have to re-transmit a resource when reloading.
items.after: For cache-busted static files, also set Last-Modified and ETag, so that a reload revalidates the file instead of re-transmitting it.

items.problem: "Types of caches" runs to about 5,000 characters under one h2, so the window cuts it and #3 opens with "proxy-revalidate However".
items.fix: Promote Private caches, Shared cache, Proxy caches and Managed caches to h2, so each type is a passage that names itself.
items.before: proxy-revalidate However, in recent years, as HTTPS has become more common and client/server communication has become encrypted, proxy caches in the path can only tunnel a response and can't behave as a cache, in many cases.
items.after: Proxy caches and HTTPS: now that most traffic is encrypted, a proxy cache on the path can usually only tunnel the response and cannot cache it.

items.problem: The browser-compatibility widget becomes the words "Browser Support / Source" three times; the passage says nothing a retriever can quote.
items.fix: State the support in a sentence and keep the widget out of the extracted text (or give it an accessible text summary).
items.before: Cache-Control Browser Support Source ETag Browser Support Source Last-Modified Browser Support Source
items.after: Cache-Control, ETag and Last-Modified are supported in all major browsers.

items.problem: "Appendix: Cache-Control flowchart" is an image with a 60-character caption; the decision it draws never reaches the text.
items.fix: Write the flowchart's decisions as a short list under the image.
items.before: The decision process for setting your Cache-Control headers.
items.after: Choosing Cache-Control: if the response must never be reused, use no-store; if it must be checked every time, use no-cache; otherwise use private (browser only) or public, with a max-age that matches how often it changes.

items.problem: The meta description is double-escaped, so passage #0 stores the literal text "browser's".
items.before: The browser's HTTP Cache is your first line of defense against unnecessary network requests.
items.after: The browser's HTTP cache is your first line of defense against unnecessary network requests.
